analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: changelog.d/qwen-gdn-prompt-kernel.md (new, lines 1-4) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (date bump at line 3, new section 'GDN prompt kernels by GPU' inserted after line 525). No executable code, wire protocol, attestation, authorization, key-handling or storage logic is changed in the supplied evidence.

The docs describe a Gated DeltaNet prompt-prefill kernel change (a four-row kernel, probed on the GPU for bit-exactness against the stock kernel, with the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED=0 rollback). That implementation (libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../GatedDelta.swift, GatedDeltaPrefill.probe) is not in this batch, so the claims of bit-exactness, unchanged recurrent checkpoints and fp32 state are unverified here. The relevant threat context is TB-007 (inference engine) and T-041 (prefix cache / checkpoints). Bit-identical outputs would leave prefix-cache checkpoint contents and the at-rest posture unchanged. If the probe's bit-exact selection were wrong, the result would be a correctness issue (T-007-style output integrity), not a confidentiality regression.

The docs state that the probe allocates transiently, up to about 16 MiB, once per kernel instantiation, and that no capacity, quotation or KV grant fields change. This is a memory-model claim that the code review pass should confirm against the platform admission contract; it is not a regression visible in the docs. The claim that `darkbloom start` forwards the env var to the background provider is also a code behavior to verify (the env-forwarding code was not supplied). Forwarding an environment toggle is an operator-controlled setting that only restores the stock kernel, so it adds no consumer-reachable surface.

No findings. needs_deeper_review is set because the actual kernel and probe code is not in this batch; the docs-only conclusion does not clear that code.
